description: The Reach has exactly ten known floors, each a territory with its own rulers. For the next ascent, gather your breath into a single point—and let the obstacle, not your resolve, shatter.

effects.text: Deal 12 damage to one enemy you choose.

loreSources.excerpt:
Overview: The Reach The Reach is an ancient mega-tower — exactly 10 floors , no more ever found. No climber has confirmed what, if anything, lies above the tenth. Each floor is a self-contained territory with its own culture and rulers. No one knows who built it. Climbers enter chasing the legend of what waits beyond the tenth floor — wealth, power, or simply proof they survived the climb. The order that rules the Reach today, the Warden Compact, is younger than the Reach itself — born out of a single founding catastrophe, the Sundering, generations ago. What follows covers the Reach's physical structure, the Sundering, the notable figures who shaped it, who lives inside it today, and the mysteries still unresolved — foremost among them, what's above floor 10.

The Verity states it as settled doctrine, not hedged speculation: Korrath bound the Trials under Ishra's will , and Vael supplies the Aether that powers them . The Warden Compact treats this as unconfirmed belief, exactly like the quarantine theory and Compact doctrine — neither endorsing nor suppressing it. The Verity retells the Spire's known history through its own lens: The First Ten — venerated as the first true pilgrims, the closest anyone has come to Ishra. Treat all three as competing belief, not established Spire history — and treat the Compact's silence on the matter as deliberate, not incidental. The theories don't stay contained to Trial origin alone — they bleed into the Spire's other unresolved threads. Aether tides, the unexplained density spikes that occasionally strand climbers mid-Band, read differently depending which account a climber favors: Compact doctrine treats them as a volatile but natural feature of a thickening medium; the quarantine theory treats them as pressure bleeding down from above, proof the inoculation is needed; the contact theory treats them as evidence something above floor 10 is active, not static. loreSources.excerpt: holds any standing to appeal a Warden's ruling. Only the Trial itself settles the question. Licensed Climbers — Shell natives selected and registered by the Compact to attempt the climb. Registration marks them as sanctioned in the eyes of every Warden and administrator in the Band — modest standing, but standing all the same, with a recognized path from floor to floor. Unregistered Climbers — outsiders, or Shell natives who never sought Compact sanction, climbing outside the licensing system entirely. Wardens and Licensed Climbers alike treat them as suspect by default — unaccountable to the Compact, unpredictable on a floor, and often capable of more than their standing would suggest.
